An electric pump is one of the best accessories you can purchase for your stand up paddle board. Whether it is your first time on a SUP or you are a professional paddle boarder, you can’t beat the hands-free ease of an electric paddle board pump. We put the most popular electric pumps for paddle boards through thousands of uses to find out which are the Best iSUP Pumps of 2024.
Electric paddle board pumps save you the energy of hand-pumping and help you get on the water faster. Instead of inflating your paddle board by hand and then getting ready to hit the water, you can change clothes, apply sunscreen, fill water bottles, and more all while an electric pump inflates your iSUP.
Electric SUP Pumps are designed specifically for the challenges of inflating a paddle board. They have two stages: a high-flow/low-pressure stage to inflate the board from flat to about 1 PSI and then a low-flow/high-pressure stage that brings your paddle board to its final pressure. Each pump has an automatic cutoff that you can set to your desired pressure. Once the board reaches that pressure, the pump will automatically turn off to prevent over-pressurizing your board.
In the past, electric SUP pumps have required you to connect directly to your car’s battery or plug into a 12v socket (“cigarette lighter”) in your car. But now, many electric pumps with built-in lithium-ion batteries can inflate multiple paddle boards extremely quickly.
Choosing the best electric pump for your paddle board boils down to whether you are looking for speed, portability, ease of use, or a bit of all three. We tested several electric SUP pumps for speed, usability, portability, and other measures. Here is our list of the Best iSUP Pumps.

Features and Usability:
The Shark III comes with all the bells and whistles you could hope for. The pump itself has, of course, automatic inflation and deflation capabilities and can bring your board up to 20 PSI. It has an onboard active cooling system and a large LCD Display screen. However, like the Cachalot 2S, the screen is difficult to read in bright daylight.
You can control the pump’s settings with the four buttons located on the top of the pump. The screen indicates battery life remaining with color indicators around the edge of the screen. The Shark III also has different settings for inflating SUPs, Kites/Wings, and Air Mattresses, as well as a memory function to recall your preferred settings.
The biggest downside of the Shark III is its size. At 6.5 pounds and with a voluminous shape, it’s hard to forget where you put the pump.
Inflation Speed:
The Shark III takes over the top spot for the fastest electric pump we’ve reviewed, inflating our test board to 15 PSI in an average of 5 minutes.
Battery and Other Accessories:
The internal 74Wh battery has enough juice to reliably inflate three paddle boards. When the battery gets low, you can plug the Shark III into a 12v power source to operate the pump, though it inflates at a much slower speed than with the battery. The USB-C port can also charge your phone and other devices.
Bottom Line: The Outdoor Master Shark 3 is an ultra-fast and versatile rechargeable electric pump.

Instead of inflating your paddle board by hand and then getting ready to hit the water, you can change clothes, apply sunscreen, fill water bottles, and more all while an electric pump inflates your iSUP.
Electric SUP Pumps are designed specifically for the challenges of inflating a paddle board. They have two stages: a high-flow/low-pressure stage to inflate the board from flat to about 1 PSI and then a low-flow/high-pressure stage that brings your paddle board to its final pressure. Each pump has an automatic cutoff that you can set to your desired pressure. Once the board reaches that pressure, the pump will automatically turn off to prevent over-pressurizing your board.
In the past, electric SUP pumps have required you to connect directly to your car’s battery or plug into a 12v socket (“cigarette lighter”) in your car. But now, many electric pumps with built-in lithium-ion batteries can inflate multiple paddle boards extremely quickly.

The Shark III comes with all the bells and whistles you could hope for. The pump itself has, of course, automatic inflation and deflation capabilities and can bring your board up to 20 PSI. The biggest downside of the Shark III is its size. At 6.5 pounds and with a voluminous shape, it’s hard to forget where you put the pump.

The internal 74Wh battery has enough juice to reliably inflate three paddle boards. The OutdoorMaster Shark 2s ($139.99) and Shark 3 ($179.99) are well-built rechargeable SUP pumps that feel substantial and durable—not cheap gear prone to breaking. Both feature three preset modes (SUP, Kite, Mattress) for different inflation needs.

Both pumps double as USB power banks for charging devices on the water, and include deflation capabilities standard on most quality pumps but still appreciated for quick packdown. Eight included nozzles ensure compatibility with virtually any inflatable.
The core difference lies in philosophy: The Shark 2s prioritizes endurance with its larger 88.8 Wh battery, inflating 4-5 large SUPs (375L) per charge at a steady 6-8 minutes each. The Shark 3 emphasizes speed with nearly twice the inflation rate (3-5 minutes per board) but carries a smaller 74 Wh battery good for 3-4 large boards per charge.
The Shark 2s takes slightly longer to inflate a paddle board.
The Shark 3’s 45W USB-C PD fast-charging reaches full capacity in 2 hours versus 6 hours for the Shark 2s.
Choose the Shark 2s for remote paddling where charging opportunities are limited and battery life matters most. Choose the Shark 3 for quick turnarounds, multiple daily sessions, or when fast charging between sessions suits your routine. Both deliver reliable, hands-off inflation—set your pressure and let them work.

Battery Philosophy
The Shark 2s packs an 88.8 Wh battery—about 20% more than the Shark 3’s 74 Wh. This translates to up to 6 boards at 15 PSI per charge.
The Shark 3 compromises capacity for convenience. Its 45W USB-C PD charging reaches full capacity in 2 hours versus 6 hours for the Shark 2s.
The Shark 3 inflates up to 6 boards at 12 PSI per charge—slightly less pressure than the Shark 2s manages.
Charging with the Shark pumps starts as soon as you connect a device.
Both work very well as power banks, delivering 5 watts of power via USB ports. This is great for action cameras and smartphones.
Inflation Speed
The Shark 3 inflates nearly twice as fast as the Shark 2s. A 15 PSI board takes 3-5 minutes on the Shark 3 versus 6-8 minutes on the Shark 2s.
The Shark 3’s dual-stage system pushes 450 L/min in first stage, dropping to 120 L/min for final pressure. The Shark 2s maintains 350 L/min throughout.

Outdoor Master Shark 2S Battery Electric Pump Review – Features, Usability, and Portability
The Outdoor Master Shark 2S is nearly indistinguishable from the original Shark 2 at first glance, but packs even more functionality.
The Shark 2S has three different inflation modes.
The Shark 2S shares the same unique body design as its predecessor with the curved outline and concave end to protect the inflation and deflation ports.
There is a built-in handle, however the Shark 2S does not come with a bag for all of the included accessories. Along with the pump you get a USB charging cable, 12V charging/power cable, hose, 8 valve adapters, and the user manual. That’s a lot of small parts to keep track of!
However, the Shark 2S also features a new color LCD screen with a few extra features – oh and a massive battery!
The LCD screen can be a little dim in full sun, but easily readable when in your shadow.
The top of the pump has a small semi-circle LCD screen with a few basic pieces of information. Once you turn the pump on by holding the power button, you’ll see a fan icon indicating the active cooling system is operating, a set of green bars for the battery charge, an icon letting you know which memory mode you are in, and a large number for setting and reading the pressure.
When idle, the pump defaults to showing you the current, real-time pressure in the system. If you hook the Shark 2S up to an inflated iSUP, it will read the pressure for you. If you press the + or — buttons, the number will change to let you set the desired pressure for the pump to inflate (0.5-20 PSI) in 0.5 PSI increments.
The “circle arrow” button lets you change pump modes from SUP to Kite/Wing to Mattress. This lets you store three separate values for preset inflation. The SUP and Kite modes work the same (0.5-20 PSI), but the mattress mode uses a set amount of time. Holding this button also changes the settings from PSI to BAR and back.
The Shark 2S charges via USB-C, can power other devices with a USB-A Port, and can charge or operate with 12V DC input.
On the front of the pump, between the inflation and deflation ports, you’ll find the charging ports under a rubber gasket.
The Shark 2S can be charged by either a USB-C cable, or by a 12V cable, both included with the pump. You can also plug other devices into the Shark 2S via the USB-A port to charge them from the Shark’s battery.
Most battery-operated iSUP pumps can only work from their batteries. So if you run out of juice, that’s the end until you can get back to plug it in to charge. The Shark 2S, like the Shark 3, can both charge and operate via the included 12V power cable. So even if you run out of battery power, if you are near a car, you can still use the Shark 2S.

Outdoor Master Shark 2S Battery Electric Pump Review – Inflation Speed and Battery Life
The Shark 2S has a very impressive battery life, but inflates iSUPs at a very moderate pace.
The Shark 2S can fully inflate 6 iSUPs on a single charge..
I was floored when testing the battery life of the Shark 2S. I figured I’d probably be able to inflate our 11’ x 32” x 6” test board to 15 PSI 3 times, maybe 4. But then it kept going. Not once more time, not twice, but nearly three more full inflations.
On a single charge of the battery alone, the Shark 2S filled our test board 6 times (!) and nearly filled it a 7th (about 11 PSI) before shutting off. That’s a lot of work for one battery.
However, I would be totally willing to trade some of that capacity for a little more speed. The average inflation time for the Shark 2S was just 11:55. It’s certainly not the slowest pump we’ve tested, but it’s definitely not fast. Even Outdoor Master’s portable Vortex Pro beats the Shark 2S by over 2 minutes (but can only inflate 2 boards).
But that battery capacity, and its ability to charge other devices, is quite impressive.

Features
3X Battery Life
Worried about running out of battery halfway through your beach day, lakeside picnic, or RV adventure? The upgraded SHARK 2S features a high-capacity 88.8Wh battery that delivers three times the battery life of standard pumps. It can inflate up to six full-size SUPs to 15 PSI on a single charge, making it ideal for remote campsites, family outings, and multi-board adventures.
3 Smart Modes & Memory Function
The SHARK 2S features three smart modes—SUP, KITE, and MAT—for simple, one-touch operation. You can also adjust the target pressure manually, while the memory function saves your preferred setting for faster, more convenient inflation next time.
Recharge Anytime, Anywhere
Enjoy the flexibility of battery and 12V DC power. Recharge the SHARK 2S using a compatible USB-C charger or power station, or connect it to a compatible 12V vehicle outlet when needed. The built-in USB output also allows the pump to serve as a power bank for compatible mobile devices.
Fast Inflation and Deflation
The dual-stage system delivers airflow of up to 350 L/min during the low-pressure stage, then automatically switches to the high-pressure stage to reach up to 20 PSI. It inflates a standard 300L paddle board in approximately 6–8 minutes, depending on the target pressure and operating conditions. The pump automatically shuts off when the preset pressure is reached for accurate, hands-free inflation.
Real-Time Pressure Monitoring
The digital display shows the current pressure in real time, helping you monitor inflation and set the appropriate PSI for your paddle board or other inflatable gear.
Versatile Compatibility
With eight included nozzle adapters, the SHARK 2S is compatible with a wide range of inflatables, including SUP boards, kayaks, air mattresses, kites, inflatable tents, rafts, and more. It is a practical all-in-one pump for camping, paddling, and family trips.
8 Nozzle Adapters Included
The SHARK 2S includes eight interchangeable nozzle adapters for paddle boards, kayaks, canoes, dinghies, rafts, pool floats, air mattresses, inflatable tents, and other common inflatables.

SHARK 2S vs. SHARK II
The SHARK 2S adds a built-in 88.8Wh rechargeable battery, smart inflation modes, a memory function, and flexible USB-C and 12V DC power options. It can inflate up to six full-size SUPs to 15 PSI on a full charge under test conditions.
